correctness.rationale: Exact exposed-face classification distinguishes cube, mixed same-layer, mixed opposite-layer and within-class complementary opposite-layer edges. Every class contributes the displayed monomials; the squared diameter and unique two longest edges follow from standard orthonormal coordinates. Edge counts give the logarithmic two-atom limit via binomial concentration. Exhaustive independently reconstructed tight-facet checks for 20 finite parameter pairs support but do not prove the universal claims.

value.rationale: Complete squared-Euclidean edge-length histogram is a natural invariant of the canonical twisted-prism realization of a large graph-polytope family. The exact enumeration implies a motivated sharp transition near p=log2(q), from almost all edges being unit-length to almost all having squared length proportional to dimension, including a nontrivial two-scale mixture in the critical window. Ordinary f-vectors and the known incenter do not capture this metric sampling phenomenon.
